title: Prioritize SDK language support, auth patterns, and streaming ergonomics requests
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple enterprise customers and partner integrators have submitted non-bug feature requests asking for better SDK language coverage (notably Go, Rust, and .NET), clearer enterprise auth patterns (service accounts, managed key rotation, mTLS/SSO patterns), and improved streaming ergonomics (reconnect, partial message delivery, backpressure, typed/structured streaming).

Intake details: Since Jan 2026 we've logged 18 separate asks from customer success and sales. Key asks cluster into three themes: 1) Native language SDKs: idiomatic clients for Go and Rust with first-class streaming and typed responses; 2) Auth & Ops: documented enterprise patterns for short-lived tokens, automated rotation, service account flows, and an example private deployment SSO flow; 3) Streaming ergonomics: client-side reconnection strategies, server-initiated partial payloads, and a stable SSE/Websocket fallback pattern for flaky networks.

Observed impact: Customers building latency-sensitive features (voice agents, low-latency chat) are blocked on robust streaming clients; security/compliance teams want reference designs before approving Redwood Private/Dedicated. Delays correlate to slowed Dedicated/Private deal closures at the enterprise level.

Prioritization rationale: We recommend P1 because combined technical lift is medium but customer revenue risk is high. Prioritization criteria used: customer ARR impact, ease of implementation, cross-product reuse (console + dedicated + hosted), and security/compliance risk reduction.

Proposed scope for initial work:
- Phase A (2 weeks): Triage and prioritization matrix, prototype minimal Go streaming client demonstrating reconnect + backpressure, and one-pager enterprise auth patterns.
- Phase B (4 weeks): Harden Go client into official supported SDK, author Rust reference client as community-first sample, publish auth recipes and sample code (service account + short-lived tokens + rotation), and define SDK API surface for streaming in the public spec.
- Non-goals: Full-featured C# SDK in Phase B (defer to Phase C), full multi-region testing for Private (defer to Dedicated infra plan).

Acceptance criteria: All items listed in acceptance_criteria field are met before moving to "In Progress -> In Review".

Risks & trade-offs: Shipping idiomatic SDKs increases maintenance burden; alternate approach is to produce thorough reference implementations and SDK generators. Streaming behavior choices (exactly-once semantics vs best-effort) have UX implications; recommend best-effort with idempotent message IDs for now.

Related artifacts: design notes, proto spec, and security checklist links included in links field.

Owner & next steps: PM (Maya) to run customer prioritization calls and finalize triage matrix; Eng (Liam) to scope prototype tasks with ENG and research team; DevEx to prepare sample repos and CI templates.

suggested_actions: Run prioritization interviews with top 6 affected customers (sales-attended) to validate ARR impact and critical use cases.
Allocate a 2-week spike for Eng to ship a minimal Go streaming client prototype that demonstrates reconnect and client-side backpressure.

Define a lightweight SDK compatibility matrix and publish public guidance on when to use official SDK vs reference implementations.
Create tracking metric to measure deal cycle time for Dedicated/Private deals impacted by SDK/auth gaps.
